Maya R (People Ops): Quick heads up: launching a trial of 'Oncall Recovery' days starting June 1. Short version: if you handle a high-impact incident you can take a paid recovery day within 14 days. Details + form below. :sunny:

Devon H (SRE): Nice. What qualifies as high-impact?

Maya R (People Ops): For the trial: either >2 hours of active paging tied to the incident, or any incident escalated to P0/P1 with a postmortem. We may adjust thresholds after the trial.

Priya S (Eng): Do we need manager approval?

Maya R (People Ops): We set it to auto-approve if the incident link is provided and matches criteria. Managers will be notified and can raise concerns. Aim is low friction.

Jordan L (Manager): Any limits? Want to avoid gaming.

Maya R (People Ops): Yes: max 2 recovery days per person per quarter, must be taken within 14 days, additive to PTO. If multiple people respond to the same incident, each can request.

Devon H (SRE): How do we submit?

Maya R (People Ops): Use the HR portal time-off form and choose 'Oncall Recovery', paste the incident/pager link. hr-bot will confirm when it's recorded. Link: https://redwood.internal/hr/oncall-recovery

Priya S (Eng): Travel conflict — if I'm on a work trip, can I still take it?

Maya R (People Ops): Coordinate with your manager. Approval still auto-applies but managers can reschedule or convert to an equivalent rest arrangement.

Jordan L (Manager): Trial length? Will there be metrics?

Maya R (People Ops): 12-week trial. We'll collect anonymized usage stats, team distribution, and a short survey. Share findings and next steps after the trial.

Devon H (SRE): Thanks, timely. Small policies like this help a lot.

hr-bot: System: 'Oncall Recovery' time-off type added to HR. Submit via https://redwood.internal/hr/oncall-recovery and include the incident link.
